title: The cutover: jellyscale serves only its own API
description: Serves Goal 3: "Octave's features have the server they need.". D-109. It merges as soon as M1's exit criteria pass on jellyscale's side (plan §5), without waiting for Octave.
acceptanceCriteria: The M1 exit criteria all pass on main's server before this merges: the conformance check passes for every M1 capability; a client using only the new API signs in with a password, lists Films and Shows, walks a show to an episode and fetches a poster, with no answer naming where a file is kept; on Media3 on an emulator and in a browser, a title played as it is, one whose container is converted, and one re-encoded with a non-default audio track and an image subtitle each start, play 30 seconds and seek, right from the first frame; progress on one device is the resume point and Continue watching on another; a play refused for want of capacity returns its reason and a retry time; a worker killed mid-film costs no picture; a title hidden from an account appears nowhere for it and its media are refused.
The commit before it is published for good as `jellyfin-final`.
Every Jellyfin route and Quick Connect are removed, with their tooling; nothing answers a Jellyfin path but 404.
The native browser check is the e2e gate, covering every outcome the jellyfin-web gate covered that still applies.
The Jellyfin-only invariants are deleted from DOMAINS.md, and docs/status.md is rewritten against PRODUCT.md.
Octave is told by a from:jellyscale issue, with the tag to test.

Its pull request carries a ledger of every invariant: kept, removed or rewritten, with its tests before and after. A test is deleted only if its invariant is removed; a test driven through a Jellyfin route is ported to the new API and shown to fail on the fault it caught (review evidence, D-069).
The tables only Jellyfin's API used are listed in docs/ for removal one release later.
